Title: Discover History Tracking Script Error with different OS Region Settings
Message: Discover History Tracking Script Error with different OS Region Settings Hello, When one changes the Windows OS Region Format to one that the default decimal symbol is comma (",") the History Tracking for "Extract Volume" tool generates the following script: # Start Parameters self.Options = VolumeExtractOptions() #Validation Local, ScriptOptions, self.Options.SeedPoint = face3.EvalProportion(0,500008332455082, 0,500008452730343) #Validation Local, ScriptSeedPoint, self.Options.MergeCreatedVolume = False #Validation Local, ScriptMergeCreatedVolume, self.Options.ImprintCappingEdges = False #Validation Local, ScriptImprintCappingEdges, self.Options.CreateShareTopology = False #Validation Local, ScriptCreateShareTopology, self.Options.Tolerance = MM(0) #Validation Value, 4, -1.7976931348623157E+308, 1.7976931348623157E+308, True, , self.Selection = FaceSelection.Create(face1, face2) #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 14, -1, 0, ScriptSelection, , ScriptBodyFaceEdgeSelectionError self.SecondarySelection = face3 #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 12, -1, 0, ScriptSecondarySelection, , ScriptFaceSelectionError # End Parameters result = VolumeExtract.Create(self.Selection, self.SecondarySelection, self.Options) Normally with had to get this (We get this for English( United States) format) : # Start Parameters self.Options = VolumeExtractOptions() #Validation Local, ScriptOptions, self.Options.SeedPoint = face3.EvalProportion(0.500008332455082, 0.500008452730343) #Validation Local, ScriptSeedPoint, self.Options.MergeCreatedVolume = False #Validation Local, ScriptMergeCreatedVolume, self.Options.ImprintCappingEdges = False #Validation Local, ScriptImprintCappingEdges, self.Options.CreateShareTopology = False #Validation Local, ScriptCreateShareTopology, self.Options.Tolerance = MM(0) #Validation Value, 4, -1.7976931348623157E+308, 1.7976931348623157E+308, True, , self.Selection = FaceSelection.Create(face1, face2) #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 14, -1, 0, ScriptSelection, , ScriptBodyFaceEdgeSelectionError self.SecondarySelection = face3 #Validation Select, VolumeExtract, 12, -1, 0, ScriptSecondarySelection, , ScriptFaceSelectionError # End Parameters result = VolumeExtract.Create(self.Selection, self.SecondarySelection, self.Options) The EvalPropotion arguments generated with comma separator and  the generated code fails. To reproduce the issue change the Region Format to Swedish (default decimal symbol=",", open Discovery, create a dummy body and run the Extract Volume tool with History Tracking Open.  Please review the attached video for the exact steps to reproduce the issue. Thanks in advance. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Success of phase change of water on replay of script depends on steps used to set up materials in CHT simulation
Message: Success of phase change of water on replay of script depends on steps used to set up materials in CHT simulation A script is recorded for the set up of a CHT simulation with 2 flow paths, one containing water and the other air.  The simulation is solved in Refine and then the state of the water is changed from liquid to gas.  The behaviour of the simulation on replay of the script depends on the steps involved in the set-up of the physics. - the work flow involves an extra step of setting both paths from water to air and then one of the paths is assigned water again the change of state is not successful on replay of the script.  Instead the HUD for water includes options for liquid, gas and solid (Fig. 1 -  the workflow is simpler in that one of the fluid paths is set from water to air the change of state is successful on replay of the script and the HUD for water contains on liquid and gas The solve in Refine does not appear to be necessary in this case. I have attached the 2 scripts and the project that they open. On further investigation I'm not convinced that the failure is entirely down to the sequence of steps.  I have seen a given script sometimes fail and sometimes not.   For example, the script NoFan NoSolve , which is a modification of , has produced both state change to gas and only 2 states in the HUD - 2States 20250106.1840.3856.7z state not changed from liquid and 3 states in the HUD - 3States 20250106.1846.2072.7z Fig. 1:  - state of water does not change from liquid to gas and HUD includes 3 states Fig. 2:  - state of water has changed to gas and HUD shows only 2 states

Title: Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing project resulting in unexpected CAD quality differences.
Message: Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing project resulting in unexpected CAD quality differences. Discovery CAD import method (plugin or built-in reader) changes upon resuming existing DSCO project.  There is a distinct quality difference between the plugin and the reader.  The user in this case always needs the plugin to be used, and not automatically default to the Stride READER.  Any of the CAD plugins (Creo or NX etc) may be used to confirm this issue.  Let's use Creo as our example  Open Creo and let it idle.  Open a new Discovery  In Discovery, File > Open > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt   Observe Creo, and observe that base s.prt is active, and the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates plugin was used)  In Discovery, File > Insert > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt     Observe Creo, and observe that sh cap.prt is now active, and the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates plugin was used) File > Save the Discovery model, Test.dsco Exit Discovery Exit Creo  Open Creo and let it idle.  Open Discovery and resume Test.dsco  In Discovery, File > Insert > Browse to any Creo file (single part will do)    Use the example from C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v251\ansys\ac4\examples\pro\sh cap.prt   Observe Creo, and observe that no parts are active, the part is now in Discovery. (Indicates Stride READER was used) The Discovery log file proves this: Checking CCM for C:\Test\sh cap.prt Stride Convert Start : 8:11 AM Stride Convert Completed : 8:11 AM It seems as if when Discovery is resumed, the "Checking for APM" FAILS to detect that CAD is running, and instead defaults to the Stride reader. Further, I believe the geometry Open / Insert should FAIL if the plugin cannot be activated, and not automatically fall back to the reader (Due to the CAD quality issues mentioned above)

Title: Getting Different Results with LiveGX and Fluent Solvers in Refine Mode (25R1) for Compressible Flow Problem
Message: Getting Different Results with LiveGX and Fluent Solvers in Refine Mode (25R1) for Compressible Flow Problem I have a case from Cummins (Customer Confidential) where they are running a compressible flow simulation in Discovery Refine mode. The issue arises when setting the fidelity to the maximum (100%) on the slider bar—whether using the "Determine Size Automatically" option or the "Curvature" and "Curvature & Proximity" options with predefined settings. At this fidelity level, with LiveGX solver; the total pressure details monitor plot starts oscillating, and the results deviate significantly from those obtained with the Fluent solver. Additionally, as the mesh is further refined by reducing the maximum element size, the LiveGX solver produces even higher total pressure values—up to 10 times greater than those from the Fluent solver. Interestingly, when the fidelity is set to the default value (slider at the middle position) or 75%, the LiveGX solver produces total pressure values closer to those obtained with the Fluent solver. Regarding the mesh, it meets the minimum orthogonal quality requirement of 0.15, with good skewness and aspect ratios, and there are no apparent issues. I tested with both Poly and Tets meshes, and the behavior remains the same. It seems something unusual is happening with the LiveGX solver, but I’m not sure what. I have attached the .dsco file here. Please take a look, and any insights would be greatly appreciated.

Title: Explore deformation at lower values differs
Message: Explore deformation at lower values differs I have a customer case, where the deformation values on the lower end of the legend differ a lot in Explore stage.  In the above example, the higher end values (red in color), closely match with Refine, Mechanical as well as Optistruct (the application customer uses, and wants to compare the results with). Where as the values on the lower end (Blue in color) on the same location differ a lot. These values are small in value, and the difference does not seem like a lot, but in percentage it in order of 50+%. Is this due to the size preview being bigger than the deformation? On the bug discussion, here are the few additional points that came up. 1.  At what resolution are you testing? What GPU is being used? Ans:  I am running it at the highest fidelity (100%, standard) on a 16GB VRAM. During the run, it was reaching 12-14GB of VRAM usage. The size preview is at 0.2mm. (The user likely has a smaller GPU). The higher value is within a 5% error margin, and the behavior matches well, but the user also checks the lower values on the pot side of the caliper, which is part of their practice. Therefore, it’s important for them to see that match as well for them to adopt Discovery. 2. Observation by Matthew:  I'm concerned that the simulations they are comparing between Discovery, Mechanical, and Optistruct are not the same.  The deformation shape is different.  If you look at the "ribs" on top of the device, they have minimal deformation in Mechanical but medium deformation in Discovery.  I think there is some disagreement in loads/boundary conditions. Ans: T he Refine and Mechanical ones are transferred from the same Explore run. I do not think there could be any difference in the boundary conditions as such. 3. As per Rabii:  I think this is a bug about pressure condition. results are fidelity dependent: with a voxel size= 0.49mm discplacement is wrong. Do let me know if any more information is needed. We have also tried using Force (using the area where we are applying the load, and the pressure value), those results also differ significantly, and do not match well with Optistruct.

Title: Difference between details plot and final value of monitor when Refine LiveGX CPU solver run on 4 processors
Message: Difference between details plot and final value of monitor when Refine LiveGX CPU solver run on 4 processors For some simulations there is a problem with the final value of a force monitor on a fluid-solid interface shown in the engineering insights window when the CHT simulation is solved in Refine with the LiveGX CPU solver on the default number of processors, which is 4. I have seen the issue with the mixer tee sample model if the fluid region has been split into 2 bodies.  It is also more marked with a tet mesh than with a poly mesh.  If a face of the fluid body is split, rather than the body itself, then the final value is OK I have attached 3 projects that contain CHT simulations based on the mixer tee sample model.  The inlet velocities have been increased to more realistic values so that the force is greater than 1N.  There are 2 monitors for the z component of force, Z Force 3 is on the fluid side of the interface while Z Force 4 is on the solid side.  For the Refine stage the LiveGX CPU solver is selected and the convergence option is Monitored value so that the monitor values are written to the solver log file. Mixer Tee.dsco - no splits Split Mixer Tee.dsco - fluid body split SplitFace Mixer Tee.dsco - face of fluid body split The images below show the results obtained with the various models.  All, apart from those shown in Fig. 4 were for simulations run on a tet mesh.  I have uploaded zipped working directories to  \\Cdcw16rally02\TFSProd\Attachments\1260xxx\1260651 Fig. 1 shows that if there is no split then the final value of the force agrees with the details plot when the simulation (Mixer Tee.dsco) is run in 4 processors. The difference when  Split Mixer Tee.dsco  with the split body is run on 4 processors is clear in Fig. 2.  The value in the details plot is similar to the values obtained with the unsplit model but the final value is significantly lower. Fig. 3 shows the output when Split Mixer Tee.dsco is run on 1 processor.  The final values agree with the details plot. In Fig. 4 the values when the simulation in  Split Mixer Tee.dsco is run on 4 processors and a poly mesh is shown.  The final value is not identical to the details plot but it is more similar than that obtained with a tet mesh.  Poly meshes often match up better between bodies than tet meshes. Finally in Fig. 5 we see the output from the simulation in  SplitFace Mixer Tee.dsco where the face rather than the body has been split.  The values are the same.  This result could also point to a relationship to the mesh. Fig. 1:  No Split, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is the same as the final value Fig. 2:  Split body, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details monitor is different from final value Fig. 3:  Split body, tet mesh and 1 processor - last value of details plot is the same as the final value Fig. 4:  Split body, poly mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is similar to the final value Fig. 5:  Split Face, tet mesh and 4 processors - last value of details plot is the same as the final value DiscoveryCromwell

I believe a bug is the culprit. I attached step-by-step instructions on how to reproduce the bug below, and I've attached the files as well. Note that these are customer confidential files. Steps: - Create a folder to work from. - Open script in Discovery. - Line 8 must be updated. It includes the working directory where folders/files will be created. - Line 14 must be updated. It includes the path to the attached geometry file. - Add a breakpoint on line 181: ViewHelper.SetViewMode( InteractionMode.Solid, None) - Run the script. - Continue the script past the breakpoint for the second iteration in the for loop. - First iteration works as expected and a surface body is created:   - Lines are projected from body (line 180):ProjectToSketch.Create(SSel, plane)   - Surface is created when switched to 3D mode (line 181): ViewHelper.SetViewMode( InteractionMode.Solid, None) -  Continue the script past the breakpoint for the third iteration in the for loop. - Second iteration does not work as expected and a surface body is not created. Title: [Cromwell-Node-Infrastructure] Cromwell Post exceptions during nodal & monitor evaluations
Message: [Cromwell-Node-Infrastructure] Cromwell Post exceptions during nodal & monitor evaluations Issue started with Cromwell updates later than 11.0.94 memory related exceptions (like "an illegal memory access was encountered") popping at couple of places like Node Vector Query Monitor Evaluation Attached a sample  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ [Ankur] Details for specific workflow 1. Read pcas file (thermal.pcas attached) 2. Not sure if Nodesets created by Artemis are persisted in pcas or not. But if nodesets are to be created. Artemis uses following APIs for nodeset creation for temperature variable: NodeSetUtilities::CreateNodeSet(env, mesh, new unique node set geom id, cell zone, true); NodeSetUtilities::CreateNodeSetWithDefaultPrioritization( env, node set id, mesh.GetNodeSetGeometry(node set geom id)); 3. Title: Unable to select Location of Convection(Default) condition, making it difficult to make changes
Message: Unable to select Location of Convection(Default) condition, making it difficult to make changes In Structural-thermal or even CHT there is a Convection (Default) condition in the Tree. Title: Problems with convergence targets in user-defined defaults for Refine
Message: Problems with convergence targets in user-defined defaults for Refine In Settings > Physics there issues with some of the convergence targets for Fluid Flow simulations in Refine (Fig. 1). Engineering convergence (target engineering convergence) and solution stopping criterion (target stopping criterion) changes are only passed to the solver if the Simulations Options for convergence are opened in the 2nd simulation created after the change. Title: Sparse generation parameter range units not respected

Title: Incomplete circuits not detected when conditions are marked as Ignored and user-defined contact exists on suppressed body
Message: Incomplete circuits not detected when conditions are marked as Ignored and user-defined contact exists on suppressed body If there are user-defined contacts which include bodies on which electrical conditions are located, suppression of such bodies produces informational messages that the conditions and contacts are ignored but there is no message about an incomplete circuit when one would be appropriate.  If the Ignored contact is excluded or deleted so that the face pair becomes part of the default contact group, the messages are produced. The images below were obtained with the attached model, in which there are user-defined contacts between the bodies. In Fig. 1 the two ring terminal bodies on which Voltage conditions are located are suppressed leaving only a Current condition active.  The Voltage conditions and the user-defined contacts connecting the ring terminals to the wire are marked as ignored.  Although a simulation in which there are Current conditions but no Voltage conditions is incomplete, there is no message to indicate this.  The simulation will fail in both stages.  If the Ignored contacts are suppressed or deleted, the message to add a voltage is displayed (Fig. 2). In Fig. 3 the Quick-disconnect Terminal body is suppressed so that the only active conditions are the two Voltages which both have a value of 0V.  With the Ignored user-defined contact, there is no warning message about the voltages but suppression or deletion of this contact produces the message (Fig. 4). Fig. 1:  Ring terminal bodies suppressed so that Voltage conditions Ignored leaving only a Current condition - no message to add a voltage with Ignored user-defined contacts  Fig. 2:   Ring terminal bodies suppressed so that Voltage conditions Ignored leaving only a Current condition - message to add a voltage when Ignored contacts are suppressed Fig. 3: Quick Disconnect terminal body suppressed so that only Voltages of equal value are active - no notification message with Ignored user-defined contact Fig. 4: Quick Disconnect terminal body suppressed so that only Voltages of equal value are active - notification message exists when Ignored user-defined contact is excluded

Title: Monitor value affected by number of cores with LiveGX CPU solver
Message: Monitor value affected by number of cores with LiveGX CPU solver The attached very simple model shows a dependence of a heat flux monitor on the number of cores on which the LiveGX CPU solver is run.  The heat flow is predominantly in the X direction, from a high to a low temperature face, and the geometry is rectangular and so it will probably show up differences.  That is why I have given the bug a medium priority.  There is a monitor for average heat flux, Avg. Heat Flux 1, on the low temperature face.  There is also a monitor on the solid thermal body for the heat flux in the X direction,  Avg. X Heat Flux 2. When the simulation is run on 1 core, the monitor for heat flux on the face has a similar value to the value in its details plot and the value on the body (Fig. 1). When it runs on 4 cores, the value of the heat flux on the face is quite significantly lower than the details plot and the monitor on the body (Fig.2). The default for LiveGX CPU is 4 cores. In both cases energy is converged to about 2.4e-08. The issue is also seen in v251 SP1 but not in V242 SP1. Fig. 1:  LiveGX CPU on 1 core - Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 agrees with the details plot and is similar to Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body Fig. 2:  LiveGX CPU on 4 cores -  Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 (3.36e4 W/m^2) is lower than the last value in the details plot (4.03e4 W/m^2) and than Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body

Title: Gap detection standalone and scripting issues (part 2)
Message: Gap detection standalone and scripting issues (part 2) Background: Customer wants to fix all gaps found by the Detect tool. I wrote this script to take the detected gaps via named selections, and close them with the Replace tool. I found the following bug in the process. I attached step-by-step instructions on how to reproduce the bugs below, and I've attached the files and video as well.  Bug 2: Detect gap tool incorrectly identifies previous face pairs with gaps as current face pairs with gaps - With the Measure tool, check a few of the other named selections to verify that some face pairs do have a gap - Delete all Named Selections - Open and Run the gaps script v2.dscript script - With the Measure tool, check a few of the named selections to verify that none have a gap (coincident or zero min distance) - Delete all Named Selections - Use the Detect tool with the Find small gaps option and create named selections from selections - With the Measure tool, check a few of the other named selections to verify that some face pairs do have a gap - BUG: The Detect tool show the same faces as before, even though the script removed the gaps. Checking the gaps shows that no named selection contains a true gap. The Named Selections are seemingly the same as before, and just recalled from the previous operation.

Title: Index of Fan Pressure Rise monitor is not incremented when several are created
Message: Index of Fan Pressure Rise monitor is not incremented when several are created New in v252.  The issue did not occur with the Operating Pressure monitor in v251. As shown in Fig. 1, when a series of Fan Pressure Rise monitors are created in immediate succession, the indices are not incremented.  For other variables they are incremented as shown for Volume Flow in Fig. 2.  It seems that the issue is associated with the creation of the monitor after Fan Pressure Rise.  In Fig. 3 we see that a monitor for Volume Flow created after a monitor for Fan Pressure Rise retains the index of the previous monitor.  Variables other than Volume Flow are also affected. When the simulation is duplicated, the indices of the monitors in the duplicate simulation are incremented. The issue is also seen with internal fans (Fig. 4). I've attached: a v252 project containing a simulation with three 2-d fans (Simple-3Fans.dsco) a v251 project containing a simulation with three internal fans (Simple-3IntFans v251.dsco)   Fig. 1:  Fan Pressure Rise monitors created in succession - index not incremented Fig. 2:  Volume Flow rate monitors created in succession - index is incremented Fig. 3:  Monitor for Volume Flow rate created after monitor for Fan Pressure - index not incremented for Volume Flow Fig. 5:  Fan Pressure Rise monitors on internal fans - not incremented Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Validity of electrical simulation with a suppressed body depends on component structure
Message: Validity of electrical simulation with a suppressed body depends on component structure Not new in v261.  Also seen in v252. The detection of contacts for an electrical simulation appears to be less straightforward than for thermal or structural simulations. The attached two projects saved in v252 that contain models derived from the mixer tee example simulation.  The component structures of the model differ. MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - fluid body and pipe bodies are contained in components at the same level (Fig.1) MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - pipe bodies at top level and fluid body in a component (Fig. 2) If an electrical simulation is set up on the pipe bodies with the fluid body suppressed, the simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco is in the Cannot solve state with an error message, Unconnected bodies located as in Fig. 3.  A similar simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco, however, is valid (Fig. 4). The animation shown in Fig. 5 shows that if physics auto update is disabled for the invalid simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco, the simulation state changes to valid although the message is still displayed.  Moreover, the simulation can be solved and the solution appears to be similar to that obtained from the valid simulation based on  MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco (Figs 6 and 7). If the fluid body in MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco is deleted, the simulation is valid and can be solved giving a solution similar to those obtained from the other set-ups. In addition to the projects, I have attached zipped working directories for setting up the simulations on the two models with the fluid body suppressed and MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco with the fluid body deleted. Fig. 1:  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco Fig. 2:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco Fig. 3:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body. Error message about unconnected bodies Fig. 4:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body. Simulation is valid Fig. 5:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body followed by switching off physics auto update Fig. 6:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body with physics auto update disabled can be solved Fig. 7:   MixerTee Geom V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body.  Solution is as for  MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco with auto update disabled Fig. 8:   MixerTee Geom V252.4.dsco - set up with fluid body deleted - no messages and solution similar to previous

Title: Underprediction of total pressure (node-average) in apollo
Message: Underprediction of total pressure (node-average) in apollo The average of total pressure obtaining using 'QuerySurfaceResultsAsPointCloud' function is lower than the average value obtained from Fluent (using both Apollo and Refine meshes) Example 1: Simple Box - Fluid Only For a simple setup of a fluid only case using a cube of unit length (1m), when solved in Apollo, is showing a significantly lower total pressure  Breakdown of total pressure average values on individual walls When we export a csv of the values obtained from using  'QuerySurfaceResultsAsPointCloud' function in Apollo, we see that the node distribution in the csv data is not uniform (the box setup should result in a uniform distribution of nodes as we can see in the mesh). The number of nodes are not similar on parallel faces. When we export the solution data from Fluent (using the Apollo mesh), we can see the anticipated uniform distribution of nodes (approx. 8500-8850 nodes on each surface of the cube) For the outlet, top wall and front wall, the nodes distribution is halting at a co-ordinate value of 0.601m and not extending up to 1m. Example 2:  Simple 2 Boxes - CHT The total pressure average values for all the faces in the fluid volume are as follows: The difference in results is not as drastic as example 1 but we can see a similar trend of underprediction of average values and non-uniform distribution of nodes on parallel faces PS: 1) Ensured that the solver converges for both examples in Apollo and Fluent 2) The averaging of total pressure is done as follows:             Average = Sum of total pressure / Number of nodes 3) Marked the bug as high priority as we are seeing inconsistencies with simple models at the moment. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug

Title: Explore coupled solver affects value of pressure drop in converged simulation
Message: Explore coupled solver affects value of pressure drop in converged simulation Causes failure of regression test, Fluid Compressible EditBCs Started with  2025-07-31 08:16 P00 In the test the expected value for the pressure drop monitor in Explore is 1402.67 Pa when the solver has converged to the default target of 0.01.  However, with the coupled solver it is now  2633.234 Pa.  If the target is tightened to 0.0001, the pressure drop decreases to 1415.69 Pa, i.e. closer to the expected value, which was obtained with the segregated solver with the looser target.  The values of the velocity/Mach no. monitors are also more similar to the expected values when the convergence target is tightened for the coupled solver. The journal with a **break just before the Explore solve and the geometry file are attached.  I have attached Live Solver logs obtained with the coupled solvers for targets of 0.01 and 0.0001.  I have also attached the log for the SIMPLE segregated solver with a target of 0.01.  They show that:  the coupled solver with the default target is deemed to have converged after 366 iterations the coupled solver with the tightened target after 1360 iterations the segregated solver with the default target after 1693 iterations Disco Regression

Title: Difference in coordinate systems in Discovery
Message: Difference in coordinate systems in Discovery A discrepancy in coordinates has been observed when checking the geometry of a customer’s model. The customer noticed a small gap in the geometry while using Fluent. Upon further investigation, they found that the coordinates in the global model differ from those when opening local components separately. Specifically, the coordinates for vertices in different components (CADFEM Support and Fluid plates) are not consistent. CP and I tested the issue on my end and am noticing the same behavior. I opened the geometry, selected a random vertex, and checked the world origin (x, y, z coordinates). We found a slight difference in the decimal values for the coordinates of the same vertex in the two components. In the CADFEM Support file, the X coordinate of the selected vertex is 239.8713 mm . In the Fluid plates file, the X coordinate of the same vertex is 239.8899 mm . Steps to Replicate: Open the file Activate the world origin Go to the Measure tab. Choose any random vertex on the CADFEM Support component. Record the X, Y, and Z coordinates at the world origin (note any decimal differences). Repeat the process for the Fluid plates component, selecting the sameand noting the X, Y, and Z coordinates.

Title: Synchronization with Live is happening twice at different times when toggling Capture Sharp Edges option
Message: Synchronization with Live is happening twice at different times when toggling Capture Sharp Edges option There are two places handling resync with Live when Capture Sharp Edges option is toggled. The one in ApplySimulation happens first, but then GeometryCaching clears and resyncs again. A side problem with that is the booleaned body's Id map is regenerated. But ordering of the body in the Linq statement is not guaranteed, the Ids are changed on regeneration (even if bodies and faces are the same). Physics are resync'd after that so they should be OK.

Title: Different types of messages about missing voltage conditions depending on type of existing condition
Message: Different types of messages about missing voltage conditions depending on type of existing condition The attached project contains a thermal electrical simulation based on the buss bar model in the parts directory.  As shown in Fig. 1, on one end of the body called Load 4, there is a current condition and it is connected to MainBus3 by Bonded Contact 1.  Voltage 4 is on one end of Load 2, which is connected to MainBus3 by Bonded Contact 3. If Bonded Contact 1 is made an electrical insulator, there is an informational message that a voltage condition is required (Fig.2).  The simulation state is not fully defined yet. However, if Bonded 3 is made an electrical insulator, the message to add a voltage or a current is an error message and the state is Cannot Solve. Shouldn't both messages be informational and the state be not fully defined yet? Also the message to Add a voltage includes a link that opens up a voltage condition but there are no such links in the message to Add a voltage or a current. Fig. 1:  Thermal electrical buss bar simulation Fig. 2:  Informational message when Bonded Contact 1 is an insulator and a voltage condition is required Fig. 3:  Error message when Bonded Contact 3 is an electrical insulator and a current or a voltage is required

Title: Bringing up the HUD for materials takes 6-7 seconds when Algoryx add-in is loaded
Message: Bringing up the HUD for materials takes 6-7 seconds when Algoryx add-in is loaded Bring up the material HUD is almost instantaneous but when Algoryx add-in is loaded it takes 6-7 seconds. The reason for the slowdown is the initialization of mediators done on the fly when the HUD is opened (for the purpose of collecting custom properties).  The problem had not reported so far and is probably due to the fact that Algoryx dll that contains the add-in is very large. While it could be broken up for other performance reasons as well, the initialization of mediators can only be done once.

Title: agdb geometry fails: ''The model contains BladeEditor features which are not licensed''
Message: agdb geometry fails: ''The model contains BladeEditor features which are not licensed'' The customer is unable to import an agdb geometry file into Discovery or SpaceClaim, receiving a "Failed to import" error.  When trying to open the same file in DesignModeler, the following message appears: "The model contains BladeEditor features which are not licensed. Therefore, the model will be opened in Read-Only Configuration." The customer reports that they are not using any BladeBuilder geometry in the model. I’ve asked for clarification on where the geometry was originally created to confirm this. We also tried changing the BladeModeler licensing setting to "If available" and "Yes", but the issue still occurs. There are two main concerns: If the model does not contain BladeBuilder geometry, the error message is misleading. In similar cases where BladeBuilder geometry was present, adjusting the licensing setting resolved the issue, but here, it does not. Reproduced in 2026R1. Please find the geometry file attached. Reviewed- Is not a class 3 bug
